6
Four cars, A, B, C and D, move from rest in a straight line. The cars take the same time to
accelerate to a velocity of 60 km h–1. Their velocity–time graphs are shown.
Which car reaches a velocity of 60 km h–1 in the shortest distance?

hints: Notice all four cars start from rest at time $0$ and reach $60 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ at the same final time on the time axis.
Recall that on a velocity-time graph the distance travelled is the area between the curve and the time axis up to that final time.
Compare how much area lies under curves A, B, C and D - the curve that hugs the time axis longest encloses the least area.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: all cars start at $v = 0$ and finish at $v = 60 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ after the same time interval shown by the vertical dashed line.
State the governing rule: for motion in a straight line, displacement $s$ equals the area under the velocity-time graph, $s = \text{area under } v \text{ against } t$.
Compare the graphs: curve A rises steeply early and stays near $60 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, while curve D stays near zero and rises steeply only at the end.
Order the areas visually: the area under A is greatest, then B, then C, then D is smallest because D lies below the other three for almost the whole time.
Conclude that the smallest area means the shortest distance to reach $60 \text{ km h}^{-1}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Curve A stays highest for most of the time, so the area under it is largest and the distance travelled is longest.

B.explanation: Curve B encloses a large area under the velocity-time graph, so its distance is greater than for the lower curves.

C.explanation: Curve C is low but still lies above curve D, so its area and therefore its distance is larger than for D.

D.explanation: Curve D stays lowest until the final time, so the area under it is smallest and the distance to reach $60 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ is shortest.
